title: Gitea SSO with Casdoor: OpenID Connect Setup
headline: Single sign-on for Gitea
summary: Gitea signs users in through OAuth2 authentication sources, including OpenID Connect providers. Add Casdoor as one, and developers sign in to your Git server with their Casdoor account.
redirectNote: `Casdoor` in the path is the authentication source name in the next step; the two must match, including case.

steps.title: Add the authentication source
steps.text: Run this on the Gitea server (with Docker, prefix it with `docker exec -u git <container>`), or fill in the same values under **Site Administration → Authentication Sources** with **OAuth2** and the **OpenID Connect** provider.

code.content:
gitea admin auth add-oauth \
  --name Casdoor \
  --provider openidConnect \
  --key "{{clientId}}" \
  --secret "{{clientSecret}}" \
  --auto-discover-url {{casdoorUrl}}/.well-known/openid-configuration \
  --scopes "profile email" \
  --group-claim-name groups \
  --admin-group gitea-admins

steps.title: Sign in
steps.text: The Gitea sign-in page now has a **Sign in with Casdoor** button. On first sign-in, users register a new Gitea account or link an existing one. Members of `gitea-admins` become Gitea administrators.

tips: To skip the registration form and create accounts straight away, set `ENABLE_AUTO_REGISTRATION = true` in the `[oauth2_client]` section of `app.ini`.

faqs.question: Does this work with Forgejo?
faqs.answer: Forgejo keeps Gitea's OAuth2 authentication sources, so the same settings apply; check the Forgejo documentation for the exact command name.

faqs.question: Can I require Casdoor for everyone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Once your users have linked Casdoor, turn off password sign-in in Gitea's `[service]` settings so the Casdoor button is the way in.
